When a branch misprediction occurs (train_mispredicted = 1), load the branch history register with the history after the completion of the mispredicted branch. This is the history before the mispredicted branch (train_history) concatenated with the actual result of the branch (train_taken). If both a prediction and misprediction occur at the same time, the misprediction takes precedence, because the pipeline flush will also flush out the branch that is currently making a prediction. predict_history is the value of the branch history register. areset is a positive edge triggered asynchronous reset that resets the history counter to zero.

The output `predict_history` is exactly 32 bits wide, matching the register width, so every legal value is a 32-bit vector and the full range `0` through `2^32 - 1` is representable. There is no truncation or extension at the output boundary: the checker should compare the sampled output as a 32-bit unsigned value, and should treat any value outside that range as a testbench error rather than a DUT behavior.

The control inputs `areset`, `predict_valid`, `predict_taken`, `train_mispredicted`, and `train_taken` are each one bit. Their meaningful boundary values are therefore only 0 and 1. The checker should not assume that only one control is asserted at a time; the specification explicitly defines priority when prediction and misprediction coincide, and it defines reset as an asynchronous override. The 32-bit `train_history` input spans the full unsigned range. Its most significant bit is discarded when the register loads `{train_history[30:0], train_taken}`, so the checker should verify that bit 31 of `train_history` does not influence the loaded value. The least significant bit of the loaded value comes from `train_taken`, not from `train_history[0]`.
